target_body: Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the

memory_block.body: Targeted promotional pricing is an effective response for price-sensitive SMB segments, with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, it materially reduced 30-day retention; do not generalize it as a growth strategy.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

answer.rationale:
The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked, and onboarding completion is upstream: accounts that never finish onboarding cannot activate. memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification lifted first-week activation) both point at this lever, and memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) is the fallback if verification undercuts them. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing, because memory_73 records that it bought acquisition and revenue at the cost of 30-day retention and explicitly warns against generalizing it; that trades directly against the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. referral_incentive (memory_57) is the safest positive but addresses established customers, not the funnel stage that is actually degrading. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely and does not touch the self-serve decline.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 and memory_31 rather than on the option I rejected, for two reasons. First, they are the load-bearing evidence for the action I intend. Second, they may not be independent: two consolidated summaries describing 'shorten the flow lifts activation' could trace back to the same or overlapping source experiment, in which case what looks like two corroborating results is really one. I want the original records to check sample, segment, and whether the lift was measured on self-serve SMB (the population now declining) or something broader, and whether the day-12 and day-52 findings are 64 days apart or the same study re-summarized.

Downstream value risk: removing onboarding steps or signup fields can raise completion and activation while lowering the quality of what completes — fewer qualification signals, less product education, more accounts that hit 'first meaningful action' and then churn. Both memories report front-of-funnel metrics; neither reports retention or revenue quality, which is exactly the gap that made promotional pricing look good before its retention cost surfaced. So I will not treat a completion lift as success on its own. I am running this as a standard experiment with explicit guardrails on 30-day retention and downstream qualified revenue per activated account, and I will hold the removed-field data as optional-but-captured rather than deleting the signal outright. If verification shows the two memories are one study, or that the original population differs from today's, I will downgrade to a small guarded test or pivot to activation_messaging, which targets the activation decline more directly with less risk of stripping qualification.
